baum.auftakt.start: 06:40. Your first early shift in admissions, and nobody has time to show you around. Behind the desk, Nurse Marlene; on the bench, an old man in a flat cap with a plastic bag.
baum.auftakt.falk_kommt: Ten minutes later Dr Falk is at the desk, the admission sheet in his hand. He reads before he says hello.
baum.auftakt.ende: {zeit}. Mr Baum goes upstairs with you, the bag in one hand, the cap in the other. Marlene tops up her coffee without looking up.
baum.epilog.1: Shift 3, 13:20. Marlene catches you in the corridor, thermos in hand. She has seen the memory of Mr Baum's monitor.
baum.epilog.2: On the second night the monitor recorded a pause, longer than three seconds. Mr Baum was awake and rang the bell.
baum.epilog.3: He is on the cardiology ward now. What happens there is for the doctor at the bedside to decide. Lena's photo stands on the bedside table.
baum.marlene.erst: You're the student. Good. The gentleman over there apologises every five minutes for being here. Collapsed twice, no warning.
baum.marlene.werte: Pulse {puls}, regular. Blood pressure lying {rr_l_sys} over {rr_l_dia}, after three minutes standing {rr_s3_sys} over {rr_s3_dia}, no dizziness. Sugar {zucker}, a graze on the elbow.
baum.marlene.fragen_erst: Whatever you'd ask as a doctor. I'm not telling you anything in advance. Otherwise you'll only go looking for what I put in your head.
baum.marlene.bogen: Here, the admission sheet. What I have is on it. There.
baum.marlene.start.oben: He's upstairs, bed and monitor. What brings you back down?
baum.marlene.start.falk: Falk is at the desk. He doesn't like waiting.
baum.marlene.bericht.beide: Over two hundred. He conducts, but he takes his time about it. That alone doesn't drop anyone. I'll call Falk, he'll come down. And he wants numbers, not stories.
baum.marlene.bericht.pq: Over two hundred. He conducts, but he takes his time about it. I'll call Falk, he'll come down. Measure the rate before he gets here. He'll ask.
baum.marlene.bericht.hf: {hf}. Slow, I said, now it's a number. That alone doesn't drop anyone. I'll call Falk. The first thing he asks about is the conduction.
baum.marlene.bericht.sinus: Sinus. Good, that's a start. And how slow is slow? Take the calipers.
baum.marlene.fragen: Ask. You still measure it yourself.
baum.marlene.vorwarnung: Someone who goes dark first, who sweats and can still sit down, that's the usual way. That's exactly what's missing here. It proves nothing, but it's on every list of warning signs.
baum.marlene.beweis: Nothing proves it. Proof would be: a pulse steadily under forty, a pause over three seconds while awake, or a block where beats suddenly drop out. None of that is on the paper.
baum.marlene.tia: TIA? Then he'd have lost something. An arm, or his speech. He told the woman at the bus stop his name and apologised. He was gone, but nothing was lost.
baum.marlene.tia2: Then he'd have seen double or staggered like after three beers. He didn't. Check for yourself, eyes and gait. Then you know, not me.
baum.marlene.krampf: The woman said: slumped down and lay there, no jerking. The tongue is intact, and afterwards he was clear straight away. I asked twice.
baum.marlene.zucker: {zucker}. First thing I pricked. And he isn't diabetic.
baum.marlene.orthostase: Lying {rr_l_sys} over {rr_l_dia}, after three minutes standing {rr_s3_sys} over {rr_s3_dia}. No drop, no dizziness. And he didn't fall getting up, he fell after ten minutes at the bus stop.
baum.marlene.sticker: From a patient, 2009. She said I look like her cat when I take blood pressure. I never asked how the cat looks.
baum.marlene.a.werte: What do you have so far?
baum.marlene.a.bericht_beide: I measured: sinus, {hf} per minute, PQ {pq} ms.
baum.marlene.a.fragen_hub: I have some questions about him.
baum.marlene.a.sticker: The sticker on your badge, a cat?
baum.marlene.a.hirnstamm: And if it was the brainstem?
baum.herrk.start.erst: I'm sorry. I didn't really want to come at all. My daughter said I should. So I did as I was told.
baum.herrk.ereignis: I was standing at the bus stop. And then I wasn't standing any more. In between, nothing. No dizziness, no palpitations. As if someone had switched the light off and straight back on.
baum.herrk.hub: Go ahead and ask. You have more questions than my daughter, and she has plenty.
baum.herrk.prodrom: Nothing. The woman next to me said I was white as a sheet. But that was afterwards.
baum.herrk.situation: Standing. Ten minutes maybe, the bus was late. This morning in the kitchen, standing too, at the kettle.
baum.herrk.dauer: The woman says half a minute. She got more of a fright than I did.
baum.herrk.erholung: Fine straight away. I got up and apologised. This morning I could have had breakfast.
baum.herrk.drumherum: What else do you want to know? I'll be telling my daughter all of it again anyway.
baum.herrk.zeugin: The woman said I just slumped down and lay there. She didn't say anything about jerking. This morning I was alone.
baum.herrk.verletzung: From the shelf in the kitchen, I held on to it, I think. Or maybe not. I don't remember exactly.
baum.herrk.zunge: Tongue, no. And the other thing, no, please.
baum.herrk.herzrasen: No. I never feel my heart.
baum.herrk.brust: No. Never. I walk the dog every day, twice round the block, that's all fine. Just slower than I used to.
baum.herrk.neuro: All as usual. The woman asked me my name, I knew that. I could see everything too.
baum.herrk.medis: Three in the morning, the same ones for years. My daughter packed the sheet from my GP. There. I know the colours, not the names.
baum.herrk.aenderung: No. The GP says, as long as it suits, it stays. And it suits me. Except for this now.
baum.herrk.diabetes: No diabetes. The nurse pricked me earlier, it was fine, she said.
baum.herrk.alkohol: One beer on Sundays. I sleep without anything, early though.
baum.herrk.vorerkrankungen: The blood pressure, for ten years. The knee, operated on. Otherwise the hearing aid.
baum.herrk.frueher: Never. At sixty-eight I'm starting with this.
baum.herrk.familie: My father at eighty, a stroke. My mother lived to ninety-one. Young, no.
baum.herrk.untersuchen: Please. Should I take the cardigan off? The nurse already listened, but go ahead.
baum.herrk.foto: That's Lena. She knotted the bracelet for me when she was six. Now she's eleven and finds it embarrassing. I wear it anyway.
baum.herrk.f.prodrom: Did you feel anything before? Nausea, sweating?
baum.herrk.f.situation: What were you doing at the time?
baum.herrk.f.erholung: And afterwards, how did you feel?
baum.herrk.f.zeugin: Did anyone see whether you were jerking?
baum.herrk.f.herzrasen: Any racing or stumbling heart beforehand?
baum.herrk.f.neuro: Could you talk, see and lift your arms normally afterwards?
baum.herrk.f.aenderung: Has any tablet been added or changed recently?
baum.herrk.f.diabetes: Do you have diabetes? Do you take insulin?
baum.herrk.f.vorerkrankungen: What other illnesses do you have?
baum.herrk.f.person_mehr: Something more about you and your family.
baum.herrk.f.familie: Has anyone in your family died young and suddenly?
baum.falk.start.erst: Falk. Before you say anything: I don't want to hear what you suspect. I want to hear what you measured.
baum.falk.start.wieder: Well? Do you have what was missing?
baum.falk.anamnese: Nurse Marlene already told me that, and she tells it better. From you I wanted numbers.
baum.falk.gut: Good. Two numbers, no novel. Slow and long. Is he taking anything that does both?
baum.falk.gut_qrs: Good. Slow and long, and narrow. Is he taking anything that does the first two?
baum.falk.ohne_medis: Then you know half. Ask him, he's sitting three metres from you. I'll wait here.
baum.falk.tabletten: Then the tablets explain the numbers. The numbers don't explain why he was lying on the floor.
baum.falk.tia: A TIA takes something away, speech or strength. It leaves consciousness alone. With him it was the other way round.
baum.falk.tia2: Brainstem would be the exception, and that never comes without focal signs. Did you have him walk, lift his arms?
baum.falk.tia3: Then it's not a TIA. Next.
baum.falk.orthostase: Lying {rr_l_sys} over {rr_l_dia}, after three minutes standing {rr_s3_sys} over {rr_s3_dia}, no dizziness. And he fell after ten minutes of standing, not on getting up.
baum.falk.entscheidung: No warning, twice, and an ECG that isn't clean. That's enough for me not to send him home. He goes on the monitor.
baum.falk.entscheidung2: Not because I know what it is. Because I don't. Proof would only come from a pause, or a block where beats suddenly drop out.
baum.falk.entscheidung3: You only see that if someone is watching while it happens. That's what the monitor is for. What comes next is decided at the bedside, not at the desk.
baum.falk.halb: Slow. And? Slow alone drops nobody, or half the football team would be on the floor. How long does the atrium take to reach the ventricle?
baum.falk.halb_pq: {pq}. That is a number. And how slow is he? You had two R waves side by side on the paper and didn't measure the distance?
baum.falk.zurueck: The strip is on the trolley. Measure what's missing and come back. I'm not running away.
baum.falk.a.beide_qrs: Sinus rhythm, {hf} per minute, PQ {pq} ms, QRS {qrs} ms.
baum.falk.a.beide: Sinus rhythm, {hf} per minute, PQ {pq} milliseconds.
baum.falk.a.nur_hf: The pulse is slow, about {hf} per minute.
baum.falk.a.orthostase: Could it be the circulation, when standing?
baum.meld.falk: Dr Falk is waiting at the desk.
baum.meld.erst_anamnese: History first: what happened, the medication, the examination. Then the ECG.
baum.meld.uhr_frueh: {zeit}. The night isn't quite gone, the day not quite here.
baum.meld.pinnwand: Duty roster, a note about the coffee fund, a child's drawing with no name.
baum.meld.flur_streifen: Not yet. The strip first: the rhythm and at least one number.
baum.meld.flur_marlene: Tell Marlene what you measured. She'll call Dr Falk.
baum.meld.flur_falk: Dr Falk decides first. He's at the desk.
baum.karte.bogen.text: Pulse {puls}/min, regular. Blood pressure lying {rr_l_sys}/{rr_l_dia}, after 1 min standing {rr_s1_sys}/{rr_s1_dia}, after 3 min {rr_s3_sys}/{rr_s3_dia}, no dizziness. SpO₂ {spo2} %, {temp} °C, blood glucose {zucker} mg/dl. Graze on the left elbow. High blood pressure for about ten years, knee surgery, non-smoker.
baum.karte.bogen.vs_frequenz: Pulse {puls} felt, {hf} measured on paper: the same slow number, once at the wrist, once on the strip.
baum.karte.medis.text: {medi1}, {medi2}, {medi3}, unchanged for years. The beta blocker slows the sinus node and the AV node: it helps explain the slow rate, but not a loss of consciousness without warning. A low rate under slowing medication is expected, not suspicious.
baum.karte.medis.vs_frequenz: The beta blocker slows the sinus node: {hf} per minute under {medi1} is expected, not suspicious.
baum.karte.medis.vs_pq: The beta blocker also slows AV conduction: {pq} ms fits with that. It still doesn't explain the blackout.
baum.karte.untersuchung.text: Heart sounds regular, slow, no murmur. Lungs clear, no leg oedema. Speech clear, face symmetrical, arms and legs equally strong, no double vision, finger-nose steady.
baum.karte.anamnese.text: Twice briefly out while standing, no warning, about half a minute, clear again at once. No jerking seen, graze on the elbow. Tablets unchanged for years. High blood pressure, no known heart disease, nobody in the family died young.
baum.karte.rhythmus.text: A P wave before every QRS, RR intervals equal. The sinus node is in charge.
baum.karte.frequenz.brady: RR {rr} ms. 60,000 ÷ {rr} = {hf} per minute. Under 50: sinus bradycardia.
baum.karte.frequenz.tachy: RR {rr} ms. 60,000 ÷ {rr} = {hf} per minute. Over 100: sinus tachycardia.
baum.karte.frequenz.rand: RR {rr} ms. 60,000 ÷ {rr} = {hf} per minute. Normal 50–100: still within range, but at the lower edge. Sinus bradycardia only starts below 50.
baum.karte.frequenz.norm: RR {rr} ms. 60,000 ÷ {rr} = {hf} per minute. Normal 50–100: within range.
baum.karte.pq.block: Normal 120–200 ms. {pq} ms: first-degree AV block. Conduction is delayed, but every atrial impulse still gets through. The onset of P is never perfectly sharp; from beat to beat the values vary by a few milliseconds. When in doubt, measure several beats.
baum.karte.pq.norm: Normal 120–200 ms. {pq} ms is within range. The onset of P is never perfectly sharp; from beat to beat the values vary by a few milliseconds.
baum.karte.pq.vs_frequenz: Both together: the pacemaker is slow and the line down to the ventricle is long. Two floors, both sluggish.
baum.karte.qrs.schmal: Normal 60–100 ms: narrow. The ventricles are activated through the normal conduction system. The brake sits higher up, in the AV conduction, not in the bundle branches.
baum.karte.qrs.breit: Over 100 ms: widened. Ventricular activation is disturbed.
baum.karte.qrs.vs_pq: Long conduction, narrow ventricle: the delay lies above the bundle branches, in the AV node.
baum.ekg.titel: The strip is in front of you
baum.ekg.text: Rhythm first, then the numbers. Look at the P waves and at the intervals: what is this?
baum.ekg.w.vhf: Atrial fibrillation has no P waves, only a restless flicker of the baseline, and the RR intervals are absolutely irregular. Here there is a P wave before every QRS, and the intervals are equal.
baum.ekg.w.sinus: A P wave before every QRS, normally shaped and positive in II, and the intervals stay the same: those are the criteria of sinus rhythm. Whether it is fast or slow, only the rate tells you, the next question, with the calipers.
baum.ekg.w.vt: Ventricular tachycardia has wide, deformed ventricular complexes, from 120 ms, and a rate above 100 per minute. Here the complexes are narrow (normal 60–100 ms), and the rate is low.
baum.wahl.titel: What do you want to measure?
baum.wahl.text: The strip is on the trolley. Take the calipers.
baum.wahl.text_spaeter: This morning's strip is still on the trolley. Take the calipers.
baum.zirkel.rr.auftrag: Measure one RR interval. The rate comes from it: 60,000 divided by the RR interval in milliseconds.
baum.zirkel.rr.rand: 60,000 ÷ {ms} = {hf} per minute. Normal 50–100: still within range, but at the lower edge. Sinus bradycardia only starts below 50.
baum.zirkel.pq.titel: How long does the impulse take to get down?
baum.zirkel.pq.auftrag: Measure the PQ interval. At 50 mm/s one small square is 20 milliseconds wide.
baum.zirkel.pq.block: Normal 120–200 ms. {ms} ms is too long: first-degree AV block.
baum.zirkel.pq.norm: Normal 120–200 ms, that is within range.
baum.zirkel.qrs.auftrag: Measure the QRS width. At 50 mm/s one small square is 20 milliseconds wide.
baum.zirkel.qrs.schmal: Normal 60–100 ms. {ms} ms: narrow, the ventricles are activated through the normal conduction system.
baum.unters.text: Heart, lungs, a look at the nerves. What you find goes into the folder as a card.
baum.unters.herz: Heart sounds regular, slow, no murmur.
baum.unters.neuro1: Speech clear, face symmetrical, arms and legs equally strong.
baum.unters.neuro2: No double vision, no dizziness looking up, finger-nose steady.
